newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian secondary market volume leaps.
newsitem.headline: Estonian secondary market volume leaps.

text.p: The over-the-counter free market of the Estonian stock exchange traded a big 18.6 million kroons of shares on Thursday, outstripping the normally more active official list, where volume was 7.1 million kroons.
The Tallinn stock exchange index dipped 0.25 percent to 104.22.
"The market is very active and there are a lot of smaller deals and only a few block trades that shape the volume," Savings Bank dealer Charlie Viikberg said.
Shares in plastics firm Norma on the free market traded 6.5 million kroons and it closed at 23.15 kroons versus 23.
Dealers said that the company's better than expected results, posted last week, were driving the shares.
The Tallinn Pharmaceutical factory turned over 5.4 million kroons and it ended at 49 kroons after 47.60 kroons. Some 10 percent of its stock was placed recently with foreign investors.

On the main list, leading bank Hansapank was the most active on turnover of 2.2 million kroons and it closed unchanged at 105 kroons. Tallinna Pank traded one million kroons and ended at 40.05 kroons, slightly less than yesterday.
